A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same paper with complete, readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–H. Text comparison and page rendering establish that differences are confined to the acknowledgments and reference layout on pages 10–12.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on eight simulated manipulation tasks and three real-world tasks in Section 4, plus model comparisons, baseline experiments and analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulation and real-world results in Section 4 and the additional empirical results in Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: Both versions use identical VLM keypoint detection, trajectory generation, interpolation, few-shot refinement and residual PPO control. Section 3 and the implementation appendices are unchanged.

E1.justification: The same eight simulated tasks, three real-world tasks and preliminary unseen-object tests are retained. Simulation scene and object sources in Appendix A.2 are also unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain IKER, pre-recorded trajectories, oracle variants, simple- and complex-reward RL, and Diffusion Policy with 10, 20 and 50 demonstrations. The Molmo–Gemini comparison in Appendix D is unchanged.

E3.justification: Training configurations, evaluation procedures and success criteria are identical in Section 4 and Appendices A–F. Both retain 100 evaluation configurations with 20 trials each in simulation and 20 trials per real-world task.

E4.justification: Iterative refinement, waypoint-count sensitivity, component oracles, failure decomposition and Gaussian waypoint-noise analyses are unchanged. Appendix C.8 retains the same qualitative observations and unseen-object tests.

E5.justification: Both report simulation results across three seeds with standard errors. The real-world procedure of five repeated trials for each of four generated trajectories is also unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are identical, including appendix results. Figure 4 retains mean success rates of 72% for zero-shot and 81% for few-shot; Section 4.3 retains 90%, 85% and 65% for bottle placement, box sliding and hammering, respectively.

T1.justification: The policy definitions, MDP formulation, reward and residual-action equations, and Appendix C.2 inverse-kinematics mathematics are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about VLM-generated scaffolds, learning without demonstrations or handcrafted task rewards, generalization and sim-to-real transfer.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including rigid-object assumptions, orientation representation, planning latency, controller feasibility, generalization boundaries and occlusion-related tracking failures.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, observation and action specifications, hardware, domain randomization, digital-twin construction, compute requirements and prompts are identical. The supplied external access link also retains the same target.

R1.justification: Section 2, research positioning and all 80 references are unchanged. References crossing different page boundaries in v3 are retained works, not citation additions or removals.

P1.justification: The acknowledgments add ERC support through the Horizon Europe SMARTI³ project, Grant Agreement 101171393. This is a localized text addition; the scientific prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer acknowledgment shifts the references downward and changes page breaks on pages 10–12. All figures, tables and other rendered pages, including the appendices, are identical.

improvement.justification: v3 provides fuller funding attribution on page 10 and slightly reflows the references. The method, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations and reproducibility information remain identical throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
